explanation: Compared with Claude (Anthropic), 'More than two thirds of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are simple and on the critical line' (Aug 2026), §1.1. The paper defines, for 0 ≤ T1 < T2, N(T1,T2) = Σ m_ρ over nontrivial zeros with T1 < γ ≤ T2, N_d the number of distinct ones, and N0s the simple zeros on the line. These are exactly N (finsum of analyticOrderAt over zeros in the open strip with Im in (T1, T2]), Nd and Ns. Its constant c_MT^{-1} = 1/2 + (1/√2) cot(1/√2) matches montgomeryTaylorConst⁻¹ (≈ 1.3275). Each 'X ≥ (c − o(1)) N(T, 2T) as T → ∞' is encoded as ∃ o = o(1) with (c − o(T)) N ≤ X for all T > 0, which is equivalent. This declaration: The open statement that almost all zeros of L(s, χ) are simple and on the critical line. Faithful.
